title: A second Green's function (ECHAM6) confirms the false 2001-2022 TOA trend from DOISST v2.1 input steps, but gives a 3-10 times smaller feedback bias than CAM4; warm-pool drift drives both
abstract: Question: NOAA DOISST v2.1 has warm steps at satellite-input changes, and OI SST v2 (the AMIPII source) has a mid-2018 step. A campaign study with the CAM4 Green's function (GF) found that the DOISST steps give a false 2001-2022 TOA radiation trend and a feedback parameter (lambda) 0.2-0.3 W m-2 K-1 too negative (sci:sha256:990a6603). It used one GF only. Does a second GF agree? Approach: we convolved monthly 1-degree SST anomalies (60S-60N ice-free mask, common HadISST1 fill) of DOISST, two step-corrected DOISST versions, OI v2, PCMDI-AMIP 1.1.9 and 1.1.3, ERSSTv5, COBE-SST2 and HadISST1 (plus CCI and HadSST4.2 trend maps) with the ECHAM6 GF of Fredericks et al. (2026) and the CAM4 GF. We used paired block-bootstrap intervals, an exact regional attribution, a regional drift sensitivity and TAO/TRITON moorings. Results: in 2001-2022 the DOISST steps give a false TOA trend in both GFs: ECHAM6 -0.13 to -0.14 W m-2 per decade (intervals -0.19 to -0.08), CAM4 -0.22 to -0.23. The lambda bias is -0.03 to -0.08 in ECHAM6 (intervals include zero) and -0.23 to -0.30 in CAM4. The 1982-2022 lambda is robust in both GFs (changes of 0.06 or less). In both GFs the west Pacific warm pool causes the effect; the east Pacific error has almost no radiative effect. A +0.01 C per decade drift in the warm pool (7% of the ocean) changes the 2001-2022 lambda by -0.085 (CAM4) or -0.039 (ECHAM6); the same drift over 60S-60N changes it by -0.043 or -0.008. At west Pacific moorings, DOISST drifts +0.074 C per decade (2001-2022), and corrected DOISST about 0. AMIPII 1.1.9 equals OI v2; its 2018 step makes the 2001-2022 lambda 0.10-0.35 too negative, but only the Southern Hemisphere part (0.10-0.14) is supported by in situ data. DOISST hides 23-34% of the post-2000 weakening of the pattern effect in both GFs. Limitations: two model GFs only; the step corrections are uncertain; west Pacific moorings are few after 2016; no CERES comparison (no data access).

display.caption: Feedback parameter lambda from the CAM4 GF (left; T = GF surface air temperature) and the ECHAM6 GF (right; T = global SST) for each SST version, 1982-2022 (circles) and 2001-2022 (squares), with 95% block-bootstrap intervals. Shading: range of the five references. Dashed line: uniform warming. Open symbols: 5-degree box path (CCI, HadSST4.2).

(a) Change of the 2001-2022 lambda caused by the error in each region alone: DOISST steps and the OI v2 / AMIPII 2018 step, for CAM4 and ECHAM6. (b) Change of lambda for a +0.01 C per decade SST drift in one region (share of ocean area in brackets). The warm pool dominates in both GFs.

(a) CAM4 GF net TOA response per K local warming (per unit global area). (b) DOISST minus step-corrected DOISST (in situ fit), 2001-2022 SST trend. (c) Product of (a) and (b): where the false TOA trend comes from.

citations.reason: First CAM4 Green's-function test of the same artifacts. We replicate its CAM4 results on 1-degree fields and test them with a second GF (ECHAM6): the false TOA trend is confirmed, but the lambda bias is 3-10 times smaller in ECHAM6.
Source of the GTMBA mooring SST used (through sci:sha256:9e1a3e72) for the west Pacific drift check.
Box step corrections of DOISST, 5-degree trend maps (CCI, HadSST4.2), mooring common terms and the 1-degree grid code are reused; the radiative calculation it did not make is done here.
The uncertainty of the mean DOISST correction is taken into account.
